$meta.role: The register of design and implementation decisions Phase 1 cannot make on its own. Every decision id cited anywhere in design-manifest.json or the token generator must appear here, and a test enforces that.
$meta.rule: An entry is closed only by the named owner. Nothing here may be resolved by choosing a value in code — that is a design change, and AC13 fails any element with no design source. Statuses are 'open' until the owner rules.

statusVocabulary.open: No ruling yet. Nothing may proceed that depends on the answer.
statusVocabulary.ruled: The named owner has ruled. The entry records the ruling, who made it and when, and stays on the register so the reasoning survives.

$meta.rulingRule: A 'ruled' entry must carry ruling, ruledBy and ruledOn. A decision that still blocks a token or a state stays 'open' even when an interim handling has been agreed — the handling goes in interimRuling, so 'blocked' in design-manifest.json always cites a decision the design has yet to answer.

decisions.title: Compact row height — 28px or 26px
decisions.phase1Impact: Blocks the token row.compact. No Phase 1 component consumes it; SyCollection's density modes will.
decisions.statement: Foundations §15 states 28px. The Design System's density prop states 26px. Both documents are canonical and the handoff records the disagreement as conflict C1 without resolving it — the design's only self-declared blocking conflict.
decisions.evidence: design-tokens.json row.compact carries the conflict inline as its value.

decisions.title: Tokenise the focus ring (audit F9)
decisions.phase1Impact: Blocks the token focus.ring. base.css still implements the rule, from --color-accent-default plus the two 2px figures §16 states verbatim, because §16 says the ring is never removed.
decisions.statement: Foundations §16 states 'a 2px accent ring with a 2px offset on every focusable element, never removed', and §10.11 names accent.default as the ring colour — but no focus.ring.{color,width,offset} trio exists. Audit finding F9 records the omission. Minting the trio was proposed and stood down pending the design owner's ruling; it is neither adopted nor rejected.
decisions.evidence: design-tokens.json focus.ring has the value 'UNSPECIFIED BY DESIGN'. design-decisions.json is empty and wired, so an approved trio drops straight in.
decisions.mustNotDo: Emit focus.ring tokens, or treat the stand-down as a permanent rejection.

decisions.title: Which icon set
decisions.phase1Impact: No Phase 1 token or component. Blocks Slice 6's Icon primitive.
decisions.statement: Foundations §15 specifies the geometry — stroke-based, 16px in dense contexts, 20px in toolbars, on a 24px grid with 1.5px strokes — but never names the set. The sizing tokens for all four figures are implemented; only the glyph source is undecided.
decisions.evidence: design-tokens.json icon.dense / icon.toolbar / icon.grid / icon.stroke are implemented; no token names a family.
decisions.mustNotDo: Adopt an icon library because its geometry happens to match.

decisions.title: ease.standard and ease.exit are not valid CSS
decisions.phase1Impact: Blocks both easing tokens. No Phase 1 component animates, so nothing is waiting on them.
decisions.statement: Foundations §13's motion table declares ease.standard as 'cubic(.2,0,0,1)' and ease.exit as 'cubic(.4,0,1,1)'. cubic() is not a CSS function; cubic-bezier() is, and takes exactly the four control points stated. Expanding the notation would preserve every number and invent none — but it is still an interpretation of a malformed value, so it waits on the design owner.
decisions.evidence: Verified against the source document, not only the handoff: Foundations v0.2's own motion array literally contains dur: "cubic(.2,0,0,1)". The handoff and the inventory transcribed it faithfully — the defect is in the canonical source, and the generator's duration validator is what surfaced it.
decisions.discovered: Phase 1, Slice 3. Not anticipated by the Phase 1 plan, which counted 2 blocked tokens by scanning for UNSPECIFIED BY DESIGN and the C1 conflict marker — neither of which flags a value that merely looks well-formed.
decisions.mustNotDo: Emit cubic-bezier() without the owner confirming the notation was the intent.

decisions.title: Three contrast pairings below the floor §16 commits to
decisions.phase1Impact: None blocked. All three token values are implemented unchanged and pinned by the AC3 contrast matrix as documented gaps rather than regressions.
decisions.statement: Foundations §16 makes AA the floor and requires 3:1 for non-text affordances. Three pairings computed from the frozen token values do not meet it. The values are left exactly as the design states them.

pairings.measured: 1.39–1.56:1 light, 1.61–2.12:1 dark, across all four surfaces
pairings.designClaim: §16 claims 3:1 for non-text affordances only via icon.subtle. border.strong is never claimed — but §10.1 names it for 'input borders, focusable edges', which is exactly what 1.4.11 covers.
pairings.question: Is the low contrast deliberate, or does border.strong need a darker value?

pairings.designClaim: §10.1 states 4.6:1, and §16 insists 'a disabled control that cannot be read is not a state, it is a defect'. The stated figure does not match the values: they give 4.47.
pairings.question: Was 4.6:1 the target, in which case one of the two values needs adjusting?

pairings.designClaim: §10.1 claims text.tertiary 'passes AA on every ground in the system'. True in light — worst case 4.75 — but false on the dark selected surface. Consistent with audit F10: no component or screen has ever been drawn in dark.
pairings.question: Does the dark palette need revisiting, or is the claim scoped to light only?

decisions.evidence: src/contrast.test.ts computes all 60 pairings and pins these as documented gaps. A new failure is reported separately, as a regression.
decisions.mustNotDo: Change a token value to make the matrix pass.

decisions.title: No foreground token for a filled ground
decisions.phase1Impact: Blocks nothing. SyButton's primary variant paints its label with surface.default, which is the value the canonical screen draws.
decisions.statement: The design carries three text tokens — text.primary, text.secondary, text.tertiary — all dark-on-light in the light theme, and none intended to sit on a filled accent or status ground. A filled primary button therefore has no token for its own label. §10.1 names accent.default as "Primary action" but stops at the fill.
decisions.evidence: The canonical Vocabulary screen paints the primary action "New sign" as background #2f6b52 with color #ffffff. #2f6b52 is accent.default and #ffffff is exactly surface.default's light value, so surface.default is used as the foreground rather than a new token being minted (AC13). It behaves correctly in dark too, where both sides flip: surface.default #1f2124 on accent.default #6ab894. Both pairings are already in the AC3 matrix and clear AA — 6.28:1 light, 6.84:1 dark.
decisions.discovered: Phase 1, Slice 6, while implementing SyButton's primary variant.
decisions.question: Should a text.on-accent (or similar) token exist, or is reusing surface.default as the figure on a filled ground the intended reading?
decisions.mustNotDo: Mint a foreground token, or hardcode #ffffff in a component.

decisions.title: No font-family token for either named family
decisions.phase1Impact: Blocks nothing. Text renders in the inheriting family; content the design marks as mono carries the mono type spec but not a monospace family.
decisions.statement: Foundations §10.3 names two families in prose — Libre Franklin for UI and IBM Plex Mono for mono — and states the rule "Mono carries IDs, glosses, versions, timecodes and diffs, never prose". Neither family is tokenised: the nine typography tokens carry size, line-height and weight only, so the generated layer has no --font-* custom property.
decisions.evidence: design-tokens.json's typography group emits --text-*, --text-*--line-height and --text-*--font-weight, and nothing else. SyStateBlock's error trace ID uses the text-mono token, which is the design's token for IDs, but renders in the inherited family because no monospace family token exists to apply.
decisions.discovered: Phase 1, Slice 7, while rendering the error state's trace ID.
decisions.question: Should font.ui and font.mono tokens exist, or is family a document-level concern the app sets outside the token layer?
decisions.mustNotDo: Use Tailwind's default font-sans or font-mono stacks, which are neither of the named families, or hardcode a family name in a component.

decisions.title: Which overlays contain Tab, and which do not
decisions.phase1Impact: Governs the overlay substrate and every overlay that uses it: SyMenu (Slice 11), SyDrawer (Slice 12), SyDialog (Slice 13).
decisions.statement: The handoff's §11 contract table states focus containment for only two of the four overlays, in their own cells: SyDialog — "Esc cancels; focus trapped and restored" — and SyPalette — "focus trapped and restored". SyMenu's keyboard cell names only "Esc closes; focus returns to trigger", and SyDrawer's names only "Esc closes; ⌘Enter submits". Yet the same table's SyMenu accessibility cell describes all four as sharing "one behavioural substrate (focus trap, Esc, stacking, focus restore)", and SyDrawer, SyDialog and SyPalette each carry "shares the overlay substrate". The two readings are not reconciled by the sources: under the first, containment is per-component and the substrate merely offers it; under the second, sharing the substrate confers it. Foundations §16's complete accessibility rules never mention containment at all, and §16 does not record overlay focus behaviour as UNSPECIFIED, so the design believes it has specified this.
decisions.evidence: Explicit containment: SyDialog and SyPalette only. Composition-derived: SyMenu and SyDrawer, via the shared-substrate sentence. Accessibility item A07 — "Every overlay returns focus to its trigger on close. Stacked overlays restore in reverse order, maximum depth two." — is restoration, not containment, and was not used as containment evidence. The v0.1 Foundations copy corroborates restoration-without-containment for SyDrawer and containment for the palette, and is subordinate to v0.2.
decisions.ruling: Containment is declared per surface, not conferred by sharing the substrate. The substrate provides focus entry, Esc-closes-topmost, restoration to trigger and a depth-2 stack for every overlay; containment is an opt-in flag. SyDialog is modal and contains Tab. SyMenu and SyDrawer are non-modal and do not.
decisions.ruledBy: design owner, 2026-08-31, on the analysis recorded in this entry
decisions.rulingCaveat: Only the SyDialog half is compelled by an explicit statement. SyDrawer rests on inference from its stated purpose — "Work beside context, never on top of it" and "Opens in a SyDrawer, so the grid stays visible. Never a modal." — and SyMenu on external ARIA reasoning about role=menu, neither of which is a design statement. The shared-substrate sentence supports the opposite reading and has not been reconciled away. Sayva Studio Design System.dc.html §Overlays could not be read when this was ruled: DesignSync was unauthorized and the document is not vendored, so the ruling rests on the vendored v0.2 extraction.
decisions.mustNotDo: Give SyMenu or SyDrawer a Tab trap, or drop containment from SyDialog, without a new ruling recorded here.

decisions.title: SyMenu's ARIA role
decisions.phase1Impact: Governs SyMenu's semantics and keyboard model (Slice 11).
decisions.statement: SyMenu's own accessibility cell states "menu role; destructive items last and labelled; shortcut shown per item", in the Design System document, which §11 names as the naming authority. Its contents are commands from the entity action registry, in eight fixed groups. The competing datum is a §Overlays shared card recorded during the pre-Slice-11 review as saying "dialog / alertdialog roles"; that card could not be re-read, and it cannot be universal on in-repo evidence alone, because SyPalette's own cell states the combobox pattern.
decisions.evidence: Handoff §11 SyMenu accessibility cell and the inventory's SyMenu.accessibility field are character-identical. The v0.1 Foundations copy contributes nothing: it registers no menu component in any group.
decisions.ruling: role="menu". The per-component statement is explicit, sits in the naming-authority document, and is the only reading consistent with SyPalette also being combobox.
decisions.ruledBy: design owner, 2026-08-31, on the analysis recorded in this entry
decisions.mustNotDo: Render SyMenu as a dialog, or put anything but commands inside it — role=menu admits menuitem children only.
decisions.note: Naming the role states the semantics; the WAI-ARIA menu keyboard pattern that follows from it is external convention, not a design statement, and is recorded as such in the SyMenu module.

decisions.title: SyDrawer declares a resizing state the design gives no dimensions for
decisions.phase1Impact: Blocks the resizing state of SyDrawer (Slice 12). Blocks nothing in Slice 11.
decisions.statement: "resizing" is an explicit state in SyDrawer's own States cell — "closed, open, resizing, dirty (blocks close), stacked max 2" — in both the v0.2 extraction and the older v0.1 copy. It is SyDrawer's own contracted state, not inherited from SyAppShell, which separately declares its own resizing state. But nothing dimensional supports it: §10.8's sizing table has rows for the rail, the sidebar and the inspector and no row for a drawer, and the only drawer-related tokens are elev.2 and dur.base. SyAppShell's identical state name is fully supported — pane.sidebar 208–360px and pane.inspector 280–420px, both "resizable, persisted", plus "Panes resizable, persisted per user". §16 UNSPECIFIED BY DESIGN does not list drawer resizing, so the design does not regard this as a known gap.
decisions.evidence: A full string walk of the inventory returns five occurrences of "resiz": the two token meanings, SyDrawer.states[2], SyAppShell.states[4], and SyAppShell.composition. No drawer width, minimum, maximum, handle size or persistence rule exists anywhere.
decisions.interimRuling: Declared but inert. SyDrawer will declare resizing in its state union so the contract and the manifest agree, will render no resize affordance, and the state will be marked blocked in design-manifest.json citing D16 — the handling already used for row.compact (D4) and focus.ring (D5). Agreed by the design owner on 2026-08-31. The design question below remains unanswered, which is why this entry stays open.
decisions.question: Does SyDrawer resize at all? If it does: what is the width range, does the width persist per user, and does the bottom sheet resize by height? If it does not, resizing should be struck from SyDrawer's states at source.
decisions.mustNotDo: Invent a drawer width range, reuse pane.inspector's 280–420px because the drawer sits at the same screen edge, or build a resize affordance.
